text:
Morgan Barron scored on the rush in Montreal on Nov. 3, the night the Jets came back to end a nine-game losing streak, and added an assist. It's the kind of goal Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking would predict: 59% of his shots last season came off the rush.

The rest of his season is harder to love. The Jets take just 37% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Barron on the ice at five on five, almost 12 points worse than without him. Some of that is a checking role with hard matchups, but it's a big number. Winnipeg has scored about 3 more goals than its chances deserve with him out there, which has kept his points respectable at 6 in 17 games.

He's built for the job: 45 hits, top speed in the 88th percentile and a heavy shot. He's a Halifax-born 2017 sixth-round pick who came out of Cornell. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last year. We project about 14 goals. On a team that just lived through nine losses in a row, his minutes are dropping, down almost two a game, which tells you Winnipeg is looking for answers.
headline: Barron, on the rush
